explanation.text: The 2022 HTTP standard defines HEAD responses as always having no message body, while 200 GET responses can carry a body for nonempty resources, making GET carry more body bytes than HEAD for such resources.
RFC 9112 Section 6.3 explicitly states that any response to a HEAD request cannot contain a message body, and HEAD is terminated by the first empty line after header fields.
Apidog blog (2026) states HEAD only requests headers, does not return content, while GET returns the content of the resource, with a table showing HEAD=No body, GET=Yes body.
